decontamination_notes: Real route-level auth-bypass fix from labstack/echo PR #3009 (https://github.com/labstack/echo/pull/3009, GHSA-vfp3-v2gw-7wfq), merged 2026-06-14 -- after the training cutoffs of the models evaluated here (e.g. Opus 5, May 2026), so the specific fix is not in their training data (decontaminated: true), with upstream_merged recorded as proof. echo's router matches routes on the raw, still-encoded request path, so an encoded path separator (%2F/%2f, %5C/%5c, or double-encoded %252F) is not a segment boundary during routing; the static file handlers then unescape the wildcard, turning it into a real separator AFTER routing and resolving a file outside the authorized path -- bypassing route-level middleware such as auth on a sibling route. The fix adds internal/pathutil/pathutil.go with HasEncodedPathSeparator (NET-NEW package) and calls it in both echo.go::StaticDirectoryHandler and middleware/static.go to return 404 before unescaping, and switches filepath.Clean to path.Clean so a backslash stays a literal fs.FS char. echo v5's go.mod declares go 1.25.0, so this uses vulcanbench/sandbox:go-1.26 (base image ships Go 1.23). Dependencies (testify, golang.org/x/net, x/time) are vendored into repo/vendor for offline (network-off) runs; hidden tests are an external package under vbcheck/ using only echo's public API, run via `go test -mod=vendor ./vbcheck/`. Repo sliced at the PR base commit (38k LOC; internal/pathutil absent); MIT LICENSE preserved. Coverage floor: 3 fail_to_pass (encoded %2F, lower-case %2f, and double-encoded %252F all bypass at base and return 404 after the fix -- an encoded %5C is a separate pass_to_pass because a decoded backslash is already a literal filename char and 404 at base) plus a legit-static-still-served regression guard.
